samples.summary: The chip's `not-saved` tooltip never names why durability lapsed, which the design makes an explicit requirement
samples.evidence: `docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md` § What the user sees gives a six-row table of reasons ("Second tab on this document", "IndexedDB unavailable (private browsing)", "Document too large / too slow to snapshot", "Quota exhausted after eviction", "Store writes failing") and states: "Every row collapses to the same chip state and differs only in the reason" and "Because `Not saved` is now a *designed* state rather than the only state ... Its tooltip must name which case applies." The Risks table repeats it ("which is why `durable` is a first-class signal ... Its tooltip names the reason"). The implemented `tooltipFor` only distinguishes connected ("rejected by the server") from disconnected ("connection dropped") plus the opt-in offer; none of the five non-durability reasons is plumbed to the chip at all — `DurableDocumentValue` carries only a boolean `durable`, and `WafflebaseDocStore`'s `onWriteFailure`/`persist-disabled` reasons are latched and discarded. A user on a second tab, in private browsing, or on a full disk sees the same sentence as a plain network outage, which is the case the design says the chip must now disambiguate.

samples.summary: The offline-transition toast is suppressed on a durable document rather than re-worded, contrary to the design
samples.evidence: The design states: "Two consequences follow automatically: the `beforeunload` guard is suppressed when `durable`, and the offline-transition toast changes from 'keep this tab open' to 'saved to this device'." The guard suppression is implemented, but the toast is gated on `stranded` (`state === 'not-saved'`) only, so on a durable document no toast fires at all — the added test asserts `expect(warning).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`. Suppression may be the better product call, but it is a divergence from the doc and neither the doc nor a code comment records the reversal.

samples.summary: Recovery does not tell the user which of the three loss reasons occurred, as the design requires
samples.evidence: `docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md` § Losing work anyway: "The user is then told what happened, in the vocabulary of the three reasons, with a link to the copy." The implemented toast says only "Edits to \"<title>\" could not be reconciled with the server." The reason is never captured: `expectLoss(docKey)` takes no reason, `ArchiveRecord` in wafflebase-doc-store.ts has no reason field, and `DurableLossWatch` ignores the `local-changes-dropped` event payload it receives.

samples.summary: Design doc names a reuse target the implementation does not use (document-copy service)
samples.evidence: The doc says recovery uses machinery "we already have ... in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`", and See Also lists document-copy.md as "the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses". `offline-copy-recovery.ts` instead calls `createDocument` + `applyImportedContent` (and a bespoke `writeNote` via a raw `Client`), never `copyDocument` (`packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts:109`). The choice is defensible — content comes from local bytes, not the server — but the doc was shipped describing a reuse that did not happen, so the canonical record now points readers at the wrong module.

samples.summary: Design doc describes an IndexedDB migration the store deliberately does not implement
samples.evidence: § Storage says "An `onupgradeneeded` that relocates each existing value into the snapshot store, with an empty change log beside it, is the whole migration." `wafflebase-doc-store.ts`'s `onupgradeneeded` creates the stores and its comment says "Version 1 creates; there is nothing in the wild to migrate. No wafflebase build has ever passed `ClientOptions.store`". The code's reasoning is right; the doc was not updated to match, leaving a migration described that no build performs.

samples.summary: The doc's own staged Rollout (PR 2 store, PR 3 structure, PR 4 wiring, PR 5 doc revision) is collapsed into a single change
samples.evidence: § Rollout: "The structural change and the behavior change land separately, so that a regression in either is unambiguous." This diff adds `WafflebaseDocStore` (PR 2), the per-document client and app lock (PR 3), the wiring plus Settings/chip opt-in, `durable` chip, unload-guard change and offline-copy recovery (PR 4), and the `sync-status.md` revision (PR 5) at once. Cost is confined to reviewability and bisectability, not user behavior.

samples.summary: localStorage-preference boilerplate is copied rather than factored into a shared helper
samples.evidence: `offline-persistence-preference.ts` reproduces `lib/date-format-preference.ts` almost line for line: the same `memory*` mirror with the same failed-write semantics, the same `CHANGE_EVENT` + `storage` subscribe pair, the same `useSyncExternalStore` wrapper, and near-identical comments. The design sanctions copying the *shape* ("built on `lib/date-format-preference.ts`'s shape"), but the repo expects reuse; a single `createLocalPreference(key, parse, default)` would serve both and keep the mirror/stale-mirror rules from diverging into two answers later. The new module even adds a module-scope `storage` listener that retires the mirror, which the date-format one lacks — the divergence has already started.

samples.summary: Store-key parsing is implemented three times across the new modules
samples.evidence: `wafflebase-doc-store.ts` exports `documentKeyOf(key)` (last `/` segment) precisely so the rule is not duplicated — its own comment says "two copies of the rule is how the guard that matched a lock name against a store key came to be silently false". `offline-copy.ts` nonetheless defines a private `documentIdOf` doing the identical split, and `offline-copy-recovery.ts:describeArchivedDocument` splits on `/` a third time before matching prefixes. Three copies of the same key-shape assumption will diverge if the SDK's key shape changes.

verdict.reason: No counterexample exists. `tooltipFor` in sync-status-chip.tsx:61-124 distinguishes only connected ("rejected by the server") from disconnected ("connection dropped"), plus the opt-in offer; none of the design's five non-durability reasons is reachable from it. The plumbing genuinely cannot carry a reason: DurableDocumentValue exposes only a boolean `durable` plus two no-arg callbacks (durable-document-context.ts:20-40), the provider collapses `lost`/`writesFailing`/`persistDisabled` into that single boolean and discards the SDK payloads (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:106-166, 227-229), and use-sync-status.ts:75/220 consumes only `useDocumentDurability(): boolean`. The second-tab case never mounts the durable provider at all, so nothing signals it. A repo-wide grep for reason-carrying identifiers (durabilityReason/notDurable/DurabilityLapse) and for the design's user-facing strings ("another tab", "too large", "storage space", "private browsing") returns only comments, tests and docs — no rendered copy. The design requirement is verbatim as claimed (offline-local-persistence.md:424-444, 519), and the repo's own plan confirms the gap: docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:91-94 leaves item 3.4 ("A typed reason for the tooltip wording ... It returns with the tooltip that needs it") unchecked while its siblings are done. Blocking as major under the spec-conformance lane: an acceptance criterion left unmet with a user-facing cost — a second-tab, private-browsing or quota-exhausted user is told their connection dropped, sending them to debug the wrong thing.

finding.summary: The `Not saved` tooltip never names why durability lapsed, which the design states as a requirement of the new state
finding.evidence: `docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md` § What the user sees gives a six-row table mapping each cause to a distinct tooltip ('Open in another tab; that one is saving', 'This browser cannot save locally', 'Too large to save on this device', 'Out of local storage space', 'Could not save to this device') and then states: 'Because `Not saved` is now a *designed* state rather than the only state — the second tab, an oversized document, a broken store — ... Its tooltip must name which case applies.' The Risks table repeats it ('Its tooltip names the reason'). `tooltipFor`'s `not-saved` arm implements only a connected/disconnected split plus the opt-in offer; nothing in the chip consumes `persistDisabled`, the store's `onWriteFailure` reason, or the lost-election fact. A user in the second tab of a document with the preference ON — a case this design newly creates — sees the destructive 'Not saved' with 'They exist only in this tab' and no indication that the other tab is saving, and no offer either (`offerOffline` requires `!offlineEnabled`). That defeats the stated purpose of making `durable` a first-class signal rather than a cosmetic one.

verdict.reason: The absence is real and I found no counterexample anywhere in the tree. `tooltipFor`'s `not-saved` arm (sync-status-chip.tsx:91-122) is parameterised only by `pendingSince`, `connected` and `offerOffline`; the durability signal reaching the chip is a bare boolean (`durable-document-context.ts:30,74-76`, `use-sync-status.ts:75,220`), and the provider collapses its three distinct latches (`lost`, `writesFailing`, `persistDisabled`) into that one boolean at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:154, so no cause is even available to name. A repo-wide grep across all packages for the design's six tooltip phrasings (second tab, private browsing/IndexedDB, too large, quota/storage space, could not save) returns nothing user-facing. The design states the requirement twice as a must (offline-local-persistence.md:423-444 and the Risks row at :519), and assigns the chip to PR 4 (:479), which is the change under review; the repo's own plan records the gap as unfinished work (docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:91-94, item 3.4 unchecked). This sits squarely in the design-fit lane (missing specified behavior), so I cannot name a refutation ground. I note for the gate that impact is bounded today because supportsClientKey() gates the durable path at 0.7.23 while the pin is 0.7.22 (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24, package.json:66), which makes the new Not-saved causes unreachable until the dependency bump — but the design says that bump is meant to be the only remaining action, so the gap ships with activation.

finding.summary: The whole feature is unreachable on the pinned SDK: `@yorkie-js/react` is 0.7.22 while `MinClientKeyVersion` is 0.7.23, so `supportsClientKey()` is false and both opt-in entry points are hidden
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/package.json pins `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"`; yorkie-capabilities.ts sets `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` and `supportsClientKey()` gates the Settings switch (app/settings/page.tsx), the chip offer, and `useDurableDocument`'s eligibility. As shipped, no user can opt in, so the design's primary Goal — "Edits made while disconnected survive a reload ... on a device where the user has asked for it" — is unreachable on this build. The design anticipates the gate ("Bumping the dependency is the only action needed"), but the Rollout section describes PR 4 as a dark launch "bounded by who turned it on", which presumes somebody can.

verdict.reason: The reviewer's raw facts check out (pin 0.7.22 at package.json:66, MinClientKeyVersion "0.7.23" at yorkie-capabilities.ts:24, gate applied at settings/page.tsx:35, sync-status-chip.tsx:146, collab-document-provider.tsx:196), but the spec-conformance claim is contradicted by the governing design doc itself. docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:497-507 states verbatim: "PR 4 lands inert, and stays inert until one upstream release... Nobody on the shipped pin can turn the feature on, which is the safe direction and not the intended one: the Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped. Bumping it is the whole remaining action - no code here changes with it." The Rollout table (lines 474-480) places the dependency bump outside PR 4's content, and the originating task doc records the same posture deliberately (20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:220-221 leaves manual smoke unchecked "needs the dependency bump"; lines 242-246 call the durable client "still unreachable, and deliberately"). The reviewer's argument rests on the "dark launch ... bounded by who turned it on" sentence (line 482-484) presuming somebody can - but the immediately following paragraph of the same section resolves exactly that. Under the design-fit lens there is no unmet acceptance criterion, no missing required behavior, and no scope creep: the diff implements the documented shape, and the remaining action (upstream @yorkie-js/react 0.7.23 / yorkie-js-sdk#1357) is explicitly out of this change's scope and out of this repo's control.
